messages:
Michelle: Deploy-bot just flagged a p95 regression on /v1/embeddings during the USW2 canary — +220ms vs baseline. Looking into root cause, but want to align on rollback criteria.

deploy-bot: Canary slice: us-west-2, 5% traffic. Metric: embeddings.p95 latency. Threshold breached: 150ms above baseline for 3 consecutive mins. Suggest: HOLD and notify ops. :rotating_light:

Ajay: I can triage model config now. Any recent kernel or quantization flags toggled in this rollout?

Michelle: Yes, we shipped quantize-opt v2 for small-embed variant. Rollout was automated at 20:00 UTC.

Sam: If it's quantize-opt, partial pin to previous model variant (small-embed:v1.9) for embeddings route seems low-risk. We can do traffic-slice pin to 0% for new variant and route 100% to v1.9.

Katie: Agreed. Ops checklist: 1) pin routing, 2) watch p95 for 15m, 3) customer comm if >30m impact, 4) open postmortem if degraded >1h.

Beth: Heads-up — we have one enterprise customer (AcmeCorp) with a planned EOD job hitting embeddings soon. If we flick the switch, I'll message their SRE and CS lead.

ReleaseOps: Can we do a staged-pin to minimize risk? e.g., drop new variant to 2% then 0 if no improvement?

Michelle: I prefer immediate partial pin to v1.9 for safety, then staged roll-forward after root cause. Aim to keep impact <10m if possible.

Ajay: Quick triage update: quantize-opt increased decode CPU on long inputs — KV cache lookup paths hit a slow path. Reverting kernel flags may be fine but riskier than traffic pin.

Sam: Exec plan then: manual pin on embeddings route to small-embed:v1.9, run health checks for 15m, then rollback notification to release-notes if stable. Who will execute pin?

Michelle: I'm on-call and can execute. Command we use: ```./releasectl route pin --route embeddings --model small-embed:v1.9 --percent 100 --reason "p95 regression canary"```

Sam: Add a canary-monitor watch: ```watch -n 60 curl -s https://ops.internal/metrics?series=embeddings.p95 | jq .value```

deploy-bot: Action recorded: manual pin requested by Michelle. ETA to apply: ~30s.

Michelle: Pin applied. Confirming routing table: new-variant=0%, small-embed:v1.9=100%.

Ajay: Metrics: p95 back to baseline within 2 minutes. Nice.

Katie: Good. Draft release blurb for postmortem and customer note: "During a canary rollout of a quantization optimization for small embedding models, we observed an unexpected latency regression in the embeddings route. We partially pinned traffic to the previous model version while we investigate. No customer data was affected; we will follow up with a root cause and mitigation timeline."

Beth: I'll ping AcmeCorp with: "We observed a transient latency issue during a routine model optimization rollout; our team has routed your traffic to the prior model and performance is restored. Let us know if you see anything unusual."

ReleaseOps: Logging entries: incident-tracking ID INC-6205. Assigning postmortem owner: Ajay. Target: publish preliminary note within 4 hours.

Sam: Operational checklist closure: - Pin executed (Michelle) - Metrics stabilized (Ajay) - Customer notified (Beth) - Postmortem owner assigned (Ajay) - Release blurb drafted (Katie). Anyone object to marking this as "resolved pending RCA"?

Ajay: No objections. I'll start RCA and capture kernel flag diff and KV cache traces.

Michelle: I'll unlock the canary automation hold for tomorrow's night window after Ajay confirms mitigations. For now, marking thread as: resolved pending RCA. :white_check_mark:
